title: PRD: Hosted Endpoint Traffic Profiles, Acceptance Criteria, and Launch Checklist
creator: Aisha Raman
description: This PRD defines acceptance criteria and a launch checklist for the hosted inference endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) focused on realistic traffic profiles and workload-driven quality gates. The goal is to ensure behavior and economics remain within agreed limits across representative customer workloads before enabling general availability. Deliverables: traffic profile catalog, per-endpoint acceptance matrix, regression eval suite, dashboarding and alerts, rollout & rollback runbook, and post-launch monitoring plan.
acceptance_criteria: Functional: All endpoint types respond to canonical requests defined in the traffic profile catalog with correct schema and deterministic function-calling behavior for function-enabled routes.

Latency & Throughput: Under the representative traffic profile for each endpoint, p95 tail latency must be <= 220ms for short-chat paths (<=128 tokens) and <= 550ms for long completions (>=1024 tokens) at nominal load; throughput must meet provisioned QPS targets per lane with <5% rejection rate.

Quality Regression: For each endpoint, no more than a 1.5% relative degradation in top-line eval metrics (ROUGE/embedding-similarity/AUC rerank) measured on the official regression prompt set compared to the pinned model baseline.

Cost & Efficiency: End-to-end per-token compute cost must not exceed the target by more than 12% after enabling batching/kv cache/quantization recommendations; recommended optimization flags must be documented.

Fallback Behavior: Automatic fallback to the compatible model variant must succeed <200ms additional latency on average and preserve schema; canary failure must trigger a rollback within 15 minutes if error rate >3% or quality regression >2% on live prompts sampled.

Monitoring: Dashboards for token-level cost, latency distribution, error taxonomy, model drift score, and canary vs baseline quality must be live and accessible to SRE/PM/SEs with 30-day retention for traceability.

Security & Compliance: Audit logs for request IDs, model versions, and keys must be emitted and stored according to audit retention policy; SRE sign-off required for KMS integration path if applicable.
Docs/SDKs: SDK examples (Python/TS) for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank are updated and verified against live staging endpoints; migration notes provided for breaking contract changes.
launch_checklist: Traffic profile catalog published to Confluence (short-chat, long-completion, embedding-batch, rerank-stream) with synthetic and recorded sample inputs.
Regression eval job scheduled: nightly runs with alerts on metric degradation beyond thresholds.
Canary plan: region-limited canary for 24h with ingress caps, A/B routing, and golden traffic fraction set to 5%.
Dashboarding: Per-route dashboards pinned to the Console with baseline overlays and runbook links.
Runbooks in place: incident runbook, rollback playbook, and sticky-state cleanup steps for KV cache and session state.
Client compatibility tests: end-to-end SDK smoke tests pass against staging and pre-prod environments.
Legal/Privacy: Compliance checklist completed for data retention and access controls for hosted mode; export controls reviewed.
Pre-launch signoffs: PM, SRE, Runtime Eng, QA, Security have approved launch gate and documented caveats.
Post-launch telemetry: sampling plan for customer prompts (PII-safe sampling), with scheduled post-mortem at 72h and 30d cadence.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal + dogfood (48h) -> Phase 2: Regional canary (5% traffic, 24h) -> Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 50% over 72h with automated checks -> Phase 4: Global GA with monitoring and gradual tenant expansion. Automatic rollback triggers defined and validated in staging. Each phase requires a gate meeting with SRE and PM, and a list of go/no-go signals is recorded in the runbook.
